short: A Danish conqueror who ruled England for nineteen years and kept the peace.
full:
Cnut invaded with his father Sweyn Forkbeard in 1013 and returned in his own right in 1015. After a year of campaigning against Edmund Ironside the two divided the kingdom; Edmund died in November 1016 and Cnut took all of England. He secured his position by executing or exiling rivals, marrying Emma of Normandy, the widow of Aethelred, and paying off his fleet with a vast geld raised from the country.

What followed was unusually settled. Cnut ruled through English earls and English law, issued a code drawing heavily on Anglo-Saxon precedent, made a much-publicised pilgrimage to Rome in 1027, and endowed English churches generously. He inherited Denmark in 1018 and took Norway in 1028, making England the wealthiest part of a North Sea empire. That empire did not survive him. He died at Shaftesbury in November 1035, and his sons Harold Harefoot and Harthacnut had exhausted the line within seven years.
